scope: WP17 checkout-local service-aware upgrade for an existing supervised profile on Linux systemd --user
Manifest-v3 binding of source state, preview plan, active plan, exact systemd serviceAcceptance and crash recovery
Read-only Delivery, Recovery and Automations operator attestations across preview and active generations
Exact process-local preview exemption for larkChannel and real-Lark-required active acceptance

supportedBoundary.sourceProfile: an active installer-managed supervised profile whose installed cohort exposes every required read-only operator and lifecycle-attestation seam
supportedBoundary.operatorResponsibility: The operator must stop every external or manually started process using DSH_HOME. The installer controls only systemd units whose ownership it can prove.
supportedBoundary.supervisedUninstall: unsupported and fail closed before mutation
supportedBoundary.nonLinux: unsupported and fail closed before mutation

compatibilityContract.capabilityProbe: The source cohort is loaded and checked before registry, Store, systemd or transaction mutation. A peer range alone is not accepted as proof that the required seams exist.
compatibilityContract.releaseCohort: The supervised packages must come from one compatible release cohort; the installer does not synthesize support from an unverified mixture of package versions.

implementation: Lifecycle and setup entry points serialize on the canonical DSH_HOME rendezvous lock; the lifecycle executor additionally holds the external per-home transaction lock.
The source supervised cohort is capability-probed through real package loading before any Store, registry, systemd or transaction mutation; there is no fallback that opens a migrating Store.
The source active state is captured through read-only Delivery owner, Recovery bootstrap and Automations inventory snapshots and bound into manifest version 3.
Copied state is compared by content and semantic identity rather than inode identity, allowing a legitimate private-copy inode change while rejecting source, owner, definition or inventory drift.

The preview patch is generated with a fresh UUID and new package catalog. Its runtime overlay is created exclusively inside DSH_HOME and re-derived from the current persisted baseline before attestation.

Preview composition may make exactly two changes: disable the Lark row and remove larkChannel from Health requiredProviders. Every other row, setting and additional required provider must remain unchanged.
The preview Host runs in a no-network bubblewrap environment. The larkChannel exemption is process-local, manifest-bound and must not enter persisted active configuration.
Active preparation removes the preview overlay, restores Lark and required Lark health, retains the lifecycle nonce/catalog contract and requires a strictly newer exact Recovery generation.
Lark readiness is emitted as exact stdout lifecycle markers for systemd journal capture; a required Lark provider in connecting, reconnecting or disconnected state does not satisfy readiness.
Post-swap acceptance requires a fresh InvocationID, matching journal readiness, required Lark health, exact active attestation, strictly advancing Recovery generation and a stability window.
serviceAcceptance must exactly cover the originally active unit set. Duplicate, missing, extra, foreign, inactive-substitute, unsafe numeric or target-InvocationID-mismatching entries fail closed.

The crash guardian persists same-home dynamic-unit containment intent, disable barriers and bound user.control masks before relaxing lifecycle runtime masks. Unknown or drifting ownership never grants mutation authority.

Pre-swap failure restores the source home and original active set. Post-swap failure keeps services contained and preserves current home, original home and transaction evidence without automatically rolling migrated state back.
